html:
The Hafsids were a Berber dynasty that ruled Ifriqiya, roughly modern Tunisia, western Libya and eastern Algeria, from Tunis between 1229 and 1574.

The founder, Abu Zakariya, was the Almohad governor of the region. As the Almohad state weakened he broke away. His son al-Mustansir (ruled 1249 to 1277) took the title of caliph, and in 1270 he held Tunis against the crusade of the French king Louis IX, who died outside the city.

Hafsid power rose and fell. The family split into rival branches, and the Marinids of Morocco twice occupied Tunis in the 1300s. In the late 1300s and 1400s it recovered, and Tunis grew rich on Mediterranean trade with Italian and Catalan merchants. The historian Ibn Khaldun was born in Tunis in 1332 and served the Hafsid court.

In the 1500s Tunis became a prize in the war between Spain and the Ottoman Empire. The last Hafsids survived as Spanish clients until the Ottomans took Tunis for good in 1574.
sum: The Hafsids were a Berber dynasty that ruled Ifriqiya, roughly modern Tunisia, western Libya and eastern Algeria, from Tunis between 1229 and 1574.
